Love/Caring
needs.description: affection/warmth, beauty, closeness/touch, companionship, compassion, kindness, intimacy, mattering, importance, nurturing, sexual connection, respect, honoring, valuing/prizing

needs.title: Nurturing
needs.description: The desire to see life prosper. It can bring up great pain when our need for nurturing is not being met. We might think somehow we are to blame. Sometimes when we see suffering in other living things we experience pain that they are not being cared for or nurtured well. We might also feel it in us when someone’s behavior did not meet our need to be nurtured and/or considered.

needs.title: Connection
needs.description: I find connection to be a kind of doorway into the experience of another. We want to make contact with what is most real in one another. How powerful it is to experience connection with another person and how surprising it can be to experience connection within oneself. I find sometimes that when I listen careful for what is alive in me, when I make contact with that need that so wants to be seen, I experience a kind of connection within myself. Depression is often a kind of isolation from one’s own needs. We often experience the same kind of pain when we find ourselves isolated from what is alive in another person. We so want to be let in, to be invited in.

needs.title: Belonging
needs.description: What a profound experience it can be to have our need for belonging met and how profoundly painful it can be to have it going unmet. We so want to be known as we are, to be seen completely, and accepted. We want to know we have a place in this world. We want to know that we really do make life wonderful for others, for those we love and care for.

strategies.title: Read a poem you like aloud

needs.title: Support
needs.description: Somehow it is so much easier for us to experience support from others than it is to receive it from ourselves. Often it only takes a few encouraging words from a friend. We just want to hear that we are capable, and competent. We want to hear that others believe our goals are meaningful and deserve to be accomplished. It is striking how difficult it is to encourage oneself, to believe for ourself that our goals are attainable and deserve to be accomplished. Often others have skills that we think would help make our goals actualize and we believe that if our ideas really were good ones then others would want to lend their skills as well. It can be hard to give others space to have many possible needs that they are wanting to tend to, instead of letting our minds assume the worse, assuming that people cannot help us because they do not care or they do not believe in our vision.

needs.title: Consideration
needs.description:
I experience this as a sort of social confusion around what one is needing. I sometimes think that others may be trying to make my life wonderful but they are doing it without first having made contact with what need is alive in me. So maybe they are trying to contribute to my need for support or accomplishment when really want I’m needing is connection or just to be heard. How I wish they had slowed down and given me room to share what I was needing. 
Interestingly I find that tending to the need for consideration in others sometimes is the most reliable strategy for me to tend to the very same need in me. Perhaps that experience is also indicative of the reality that we all share in the same Life -- such that serving life in anyone ultimately serves Life in all of us.

needs.title: Need for all living things to flourish
needs.description: It can bring up great pain when our need for nurturing is not being met. We might think somehow we are to blame. Sometimes when we see suffering in other living things we experience pain that they are not being cared for or nurtured well. We might also feel it in us when someone’s behavior did not meet our need to be nurtured and/or considered.

needs.title: Inclusion
needs.description: What a profound experience it can be to have our need for inclusion met and how profoundly painful it can be to have it going unmet. We so want to be known as we are, to be seen completely, and accepted. We want to know we have a place in this world. We went to know that we really do make life wonderful for others and for those we love and care for.

needs.title: Community
needs.description: What a powerful experience it can be for us when our need for community is met. To experience inclusion, belonging, and often a sense of a purpose greater than any single person. There can be a lot of pain in even admitting to ourselves that we have this need for community that wants to be included in our strategies. It can be overwhelming to us. As if it is an insurmountable task to tend to this need.

needs.title: Safety
needs.description: The childhood instinct to hide under the covers or run to the arms of a caregiver are both manifestations of our basic need for safety. It also very naturally includes the needs of others in our life. Seeing someone else in an unsafe situation also does not meet our need for safety therefore motivating us to find ways to tend to them.

needs.title: Contribution
needs.description: I sometimes think of "contribution" as a bridge into the needs of others. We sometimes just genuinely wants to make life wonderful for others but we are terrified that we do not know how. What if we get it wrong? What if we try to make life wonderful for them but end up just making things worse? It can sometimes leave us paralyzed at the prospect. Nevertheless, our basic human need for contribution I find among the most obviously beautiful needs we have.

needs.title: Autonomy
needs.description: Freedom to be oneself. Often we hope that others to give us this freedom but I find it’s also quite difficult to give this freedom to ourselves. It’s such a beautiful need when we see it in others so why is it so hard to see it’s beauty in us?

needs.title: Dependability
needs.description: Defined as "the quality of being trustworthy and reliable" we ought to be careful to not mistake our evaluations of others as if they are our personal needs. Needs contain no reference to specific people taking specific action. Therefore a need like dependability is really rooted in concepts like predictability. We'd like to know that if we expect something to happen, that it will. When other's fail to do as they say they will do it therefore does not meet our needs. We don't have to level a new judgement of them in order to see that our own need was not met. Therefore, the tend to our need for dependability without reference to others may look something like making simple plans or creating a schedule. I could mean choosing a mindfulness meditation in which we allow ourselves to notice all the things that are predictable for us: like our breath, the rising and setting sun, our ability to lift our hand or blink our eyes when we choose to.

needs.title: Commitment
needs.description: Relationships are often the first things that come to mind when we notice our need for commitment isn't being met. Interestingly, however, we often fail to keep commitments to ourselves too. In this way making small attainable plans/commitments to ourselves can be a healthy way to tend to this need without references to others. During a meltdown I once committed to myself that I would flip my hand over on the count of three. In it's own tiny way I was able to prove to myself that I do have some control over myself and that I can predict the future even if it's just in this tiny way.

strategies.title: Call a friend
strategies.description: Trust us, they want to hear from you <3

strategies.title: Snuggle a pet
strategies.description: Don't have one? Go get one and make a day of it!

strategies.title: Cuddle your favorite stuffed animal
strategies.description: Why do we rob ourselves of this freedom as adult? Reclaim the beauty of your inner child.

strategies.title: Self holding
strategies.description: Place your hands on the opposite sides of your face and breathe deeply

strategies.title: Play an instrument
strategies.description: Bang a piano or strum a guitar until you've expressed all you can with it. Any instrument will do. Let the universe hear you.

strategies.title: Smell something
strategies.description: Take in a deep breath of a smell you like. At the grocery store approaching a panic attack a once stopped to smell an orange for a few seconds. It wasn't magic, but it helped.

strategies.title: Call a parent
strategies.description: If you have a parent you trust, consider calling them. It's awkward at first but I like to ask "will you still love me if x..." and then I share the anxiety inducing thought I'm struggling with. Even though you both know what their answer is, let them say it. Let yourself hear it. I promise they will love saying it, give them a chance to.

strategies.title: Tend to a plant
strategies.description: Water a plant. Research how to care for your specific plant. Don't have a plant? Do you want one? Consider making an event of getting one.

needs.title: Need for all living things to flourish

strategies.title: Share your strategies!
strategies.description:
No one likes unsolicited advise (unfortunately), but you can share your strategies here for others to find when they are looking for them ;)
It would make our lives so much more wonderful if you did!

needs.title: Need for all living things to flourish

strategies.title: Try Meetup
strategies.description: Meetup is a website that tries to connect you to people with similar interests. Worth a shot?

strategies.title: Crunch the numbers
strategies.description: This isn't for everyone I know, but I like to review my budget. I made a google sheet of my expenses vs my income. Having a clear plan really does calm my nerves.

strategies.title: Stare off
strategies.description: Sit or lay down and just notice everything your body is feeling. I like to start with my toes and work my way up to my forehead while I'm just staring off. Reminding myself where I am in the world.

strategies.title: Listen
strategies.description: Listen to someone speak and before you answer, try to get in touch with their underlying need first. Often I find when the help I offer doesn't *actually help* my need for contribution is frustrated. Try to avoid offering help until it's be explicitly requested. Instead, listen for their underlying need and try to connect to that.

strategies.title: Write
strategies.description: I like to get some kind of words on a page. Even if it's garbage I find the process can help.

strategies.title: View previous things you've written or made
strategies.description: To no one's surprise I often understand myself better than anyone else. Sometimes in a crisis I'll read something I wrote a month ago and think "yes that's exactly it!" - like past me is giving empathy to future me.

strategies.title: Make art
strategies.description: Whatever kind. A scribble, a drawing, a painting, a piece of music.

strategies.title: Clean something
strategies.description: Clean your room, your kitchen, anything. Bring order to the chaos :)

strategies.title: Go on walk
strategies.description: I know you probably hear it a lot.. but going on a walk really can make a fascinating difference.

strategies.title: Listen to music
strategies.description: A lot of variety available to you here. Could benefit from calming music or raging music. You do you ;)

strategies.title: Make a request in conversation
strategies.description: Often in conversation if I’m hearing something as a demand I say something like “I’m needing some autonomy I think because I’d like to be free to disagree but I’m afraid that might sound to you like criticism.” It’s not perfect but it’s something to honor what’s alive in me.

strategies.title: View art that you connect to
strategies.description: Whether it’s in your house, online, or at an exhibit sometimes you find a piece of art that moves you - like it understands you on a profound level.

strategies.title: Play a video game
strategies.description: There is such a wide diversity of video games out there. Calming exploratory games, puzzle games, combat, story, single or multiplayer, etc. Once I get in touch with the need that is alive in me it’s fun to look for a game or game genre that might tend specifically to that.

needs.title: Do things at my own pace and in my own way

strategies.title: Road trip
strategies.description: Long or short it doesn't matter. Drive around the block in silence or with music. Maybe plan a trip somewhere.

needs.title: Do things at my own pace and in my own way

strategies.title: No Man's Sky
strategies.description: For me this game is calming. Just go harvest resources and float through space. I like to name things to as a way to feel like I'm making a difference or matter because there is a tiny chance someone someday will land on the planet and see all the names.

strategies.title: Schedule your day
strategies.description: Consider using pictures if lists are unhelpful. Could draw them or print them. It's not perfect but having some kind of a plan can help me

strategies.title: Reduce Mental Tasks
strategies.description: If you end up with a list that is overwhelming then see if you can give yourself freedom to reduce or combine tasks. For example if you can’t seem to work out regularly because of the anxiety of counting reps or planning routines consider watching a guided youtube video or finding a gym that offers a trainer. Be honest and try to let any shame leave your body if you can. We can’t all do everything like everyone else :)

strategies.title: Play a social video game
strategies.description: Some games involve other human interactions, corporatize games are sometimes called “PVE” (player vs environment) but other games that have compelling fictional characters could also be nice. Similar to reading a book you can build relationships with the characters and find connection in relating to their experience.

strategies.title: Read a character driven novel
strategies.description: When we read a book the world and it’s inhabitants can feel especially personal. We can build very powerful connections this way and can go a long way in helping us feel less alone in the world. It’s okay for those relationships to mean so much to us, that’s why the author worked so hard on them <3

strategies.title: Mindfulness (Trust)
strategies.description: Reflect on moments you’ve reliably done what you intended to. From things like getting out of bed (eventually) to doing chores or keeping a promise to a friend. Every moment you make it through, each next breath you take, you prove to your friends and family that you can be trusted to keep living. If someone is not able to extend trust to you it doesn’t have to mean you are untrustworthy. It just means they have a need too which is not being met for some reason. I find when I engage my thoughts this way it’s easier to have compassion on myself and others.

strategies.title: Write a letter
strategies.description: To a friend or a senator. Advocate for yourself or others.

strategies.title: Compassionate meditation
strategies.description:
Reflect on decision you made that you regret and listen for the need you were trying to meet. Leave room to grieve how tragic it is that in that moment no better strategies came to mind. 
Do the same exercise reflecting on past pains you’ve endured from others. Consider what need was not met for you when they did or did not do a specific thing. Honor the need that wasn’t met. Consider what need they have had and grieve how tragic it is that no better strategies came to mind for them in that moment - strategies that could have included your needs.

strategies.title: Make a list and check things off
strategies.description: If you make the tasks small enough so as to avoid becoming overwhelmed the experience of checking something off a list can be very powerful. Things like “10 minutes playing piano scales” or “10 minutes cleaning the kitchen” are a great start. Set a timer and allow yourself to feel repeat when the ten minutes are up. Don’t force yourself to go past these simple goal. Enjoy having make a goal and achieved it.

strategies.title: Watch a comfort show
strategies.description: Try to make space to watch a tv show or movie that feels something like home for you.

strategies.title: (Honor) Reflection Meditation
strategies.description:
Reflect on moments this need has been met in the past. Was it an award you received? Verbal affirmation from a loved one? Consider calling a trusted friend and making a very vulnerable and specific request. "I'm wondering if you could tell me that even though I haven't accomplished some of my dreams, I am still beautiful person whose existence adds value to the world?" 
Consider also if you can validate that in yourself sometimes, perhaps regularly. Reflect on art your proud of, or the children your proud to have raised, the obstacles you're overcome in life, and see if you can honor yourself in some way by meditating on those things.

strategies.title: Request a clear request
strategies.description: Consider asking someone to share a vulnerable and specific request with you? Call a friend or loved one and vulnerably share that you really are just wanting to make life wonderful for them but you're unsure how. Make clear that you are looking for requests that leave out all ambiguity. Ask if they would share what needs are alive in them and imagine ways you could contribute to *one* of them.

strategies.title: Charity work
strategies.description: Consider looking for charity work in your area. Find a soup kitchen for the homeless or a local nonprofit doing work you believe in. Even just walking along picking up trash truly does make life more wonderful for your entire community - even if only in some small and sacred way.

strategies.title: Sing
strategies.description: Find a private place to sing as loud as you’re comfortable. Sing with your favorite song in the car or if you play an instrument you could play a song you know. Search for a hymn online and sing that.

strategies.title: Read a poem you like aloud
strategies.description: Try a search online like poets.org. Search a key word related to what you’re experiencing right now. Find a poem you’re relating to and in the privacy of your room or car or closet (wherever you feel comfortable) and read the poem aloud to yourself. Let it gives you words in a time when you have none. Experience the validation that this artist understands also how you might be feeling right now and sees it as valid too.

strategies.title: Stand Largely
strategies.description: Take a wide stance, place your arms up high and apart. Making a sort of X shape with your arms and legs take up as much space as possible. Trying this for about 30 seconds. We know that the postures our bodies takes often represent our emotional state and, interestingly, research suggests that this system can also work in reverse. Give your body space and see if it helps give your psychological date space too.

strategies.title: Volunteering / Acts of Kindness
strategies.description: Tend to the life in others. Looks for ways that seem like trustworthy strategies to truly make life more wonderful for others. Sometimes we find that serving life in others turns out to serve life in us as well. Be careful to truly hear and identify what someone is needing before you try to do something you think they'd enjoy as it can turn out to be especially discouraging to have tried to make life wonderful for someone only to realize they were needing something else altogether. Make space for them to share their needs and make a clear request or seek out volunteer work that are confident really is doing good work.

strategies.title: Sip water slowly
strategies.description: Pause and take ten tiny sips, noticing the temperature and sensation.

strategies.title: Neck release
strategies.description: Roll your head in small circles; then tilt ear to shoulder for three breaths each side.

strategies.title: Shoulder rolls
strategies.description: Roll shoulders forward ten times, then back ten times, noticing any change.

strategies.title: Shake for 30 seconds
strategies.description: Set a timer and gently shake arms, hands, and legs to discharge tension.

strategies.title: Wall push-ups
strategies.description: Do five slow wall push-ups; feel your strength and breathing.

strategies.title: Back to wall lean
strategies.description: Press your spine to a wall and breathe into your back for 5 breaths.

strategies.title: Butterfly taps
strategies.description: Cross arms over chest and tap alternately left/right for 60 seconds.

strategies.title: Hand on heart breaths
strategies.description: Place a palm on your chest; inhale for 4, exhale for 6, five times.

strategies.title: Box breathing
strategies.description: Trace a square with your finger: inhale 4, hold 4, exhale 4, hold 4 (4 rounds).

strategies.title: 4-7-8 breathing
strategies.description: Inhale 4, hold 7, exhale 8 (four cycles).

strategies.title: Alternate-nostril breaths
strategies.description: Gently alternate closing nostrils; breathe through one, then the other.

strategies.title: Count 20 exhalations
strategies.description: Silently count only the out-breaths from 1 to 20. If you lose count, restart.

strategies.title: Legs up the wall
strategies.description: Lay with calves on a chair or wall for two minutes.

strategies.title: Floor starfish
strategies.description: Lay flat, arms and legs wide, and let the floor hold you for one minute.

strategies.title: Soft-gaze minute
strategies.description: Choose one spot and rest your gaze there for 60 seconds.

strategies.title: 5-4-3-2-1 check
strategies.description: Name 5 things you see, 4 feel, 3 hear, 2 smell, 1 taste.

strategies.title: Color hunt
strategies.description: Pick one color and find five items of that color around you.

strategies.title: Window minute
strategies.description: Open a window and take five fuller breaths of outside air.

strategies.title: Step outside briefly
strategies.description: Step outside (or to a doorway) and notice temperature and light.

strategies.title: Feel your feet
strategies.description: Place both feet flat; press toes, heels, edges; notice contact.

strategies.title: Barefoot on grass
strategies.description: If available, stand barefoot on grass or carpet for 30 seconds.

strategies.title: Hold something cool
strategies.description: Hold a cool object or an ice cube and notice the sensation for 20 seconds.

strategies.title: Sky glance
strategies.description: Look up at the sky and track one cloud or patch of blue for 30 seconds.

strategies.title: Name three sounds
strategies.description: Listen and name three distinct sounds near or far.

strategies.title: Trace an object
strategies.description: With your finger, trace the outline of any object slowly.

strategies.title: One-minute doodle
strategies.description: Draw lines, dots, or shapes continuously for 60 seconds.

strategies.title: Write three sentences
strategies.description: Write three unedited sentences about “right now.”

strategies.title: Haiku in a minute
strategies.description: Write a 5-7-5 poem about what you notice.

strategies.title: Name three needs alive
strategies.description: Write down three needs that feel alive for you in this moment.

strategies.title: Observation only
strategies.description: Write one sentence describing what happened with zero evaluations.

strategies.title: Translate a “should”
strategies.description: Rewrite one “I should…” as “I choose to… because I value…”.

strategies.title: Micro-request to self
strategies.description: Write one tiny, do-now request you can meet in 2 minutes.

strategies.title: Unsended appreciation
strategies.description: Write a 2-sentence appreciation to yourself; keep it.

strategies.title: Needs → strategies map
strategies.description: List one need and brainstorm three different strategies for it.

strategies.title: Circle the priority
strategies.description: List five needs and circle one to tend in the next ten minutes.

strategies.title: Name a limit kindly
strategies.description: Say aloud: “I’m not ready to decide yet.”

strategies.title: Ask for a pause
strategies.description: Say: “Could we take a 5-minute pause and return at :15?”

strategies.title: Ask for channel shift
strategies.description: Say: “Could we move this to text so I can think?”

strategies.title: Ask for specifics
strategies.description: Say: “What would this look like in concrete steps?”

strategies.title: Turn on Do Not Disturb
strategies.description: Set DND for 10 minutes; return when the timer ends.

strategies.title: Phone face-down
strategies.description: Place phone face-down/out of reach for five minutes.

strategies.title: One thing off today
strategies.description: Choose one nonessential thing you will not do today.

strategies.title: Two-minute eye rest
strategies.description: Close eyes or look at a far point for two minutes.

strategies.title: Jaw unclench
strategies.description: Place tongue on the floor of your mouth; relax jaw for 10 breaths.

strategies.title: Peripheral vision soften
strategies.description: Widen your visual field to the edges for 30 seconds.

strategies.title: Gentle sway
strategies.description: Stand or sit and sway side-to-side with your breath.

strategies.title: Slow-walk 60 seconds
strategies.description: Walk deliberately slowly for one minute, feeling each step.

strategies.title: Texture touch
strategies.description: Touch wood, fabric, or stone; describe the texture to yourself.

strategies.title: Wrap in a blanket
strategies.description: Wrap shoulders and torso; notice warmth and weight.

strategies.title: Pillow nest
strategies.description: Create a quick cushion “nest” behind your back or under knees.

strategies.title: Light adjust
strategies.description: Increase or dim the light to suit your body right now.

strategies.title: Open the blinds
strategies.description: Let natural light in and look outside for 30 seconds.

strategies.title: Fresh socks
strategies.description: Change into clean or cozy socks for a reset.

strategies.title: Posture reset
strategies.description: Sit or stand tall; lengthen spine; soften shoulders.

strategies.title: One kind text
strategies.description: Send “Thinking of you—no need to reply.” to someone you trust.

strategies.title: Specific thank-you
strategies.description: Send a short note naming one action someone did and how it supported you.

strategies.title: Kind comment online
strategies.description: Leave a brief, sincere encouragement on a post.

strategies.title: Mirror kindness
strategies.description: Look in a mirror and say one thing you appreciate about your effort today.

strategies.title: Count backward from 30
strategies.description: Count down slowly; notice your breath syncing with the count.

strategies.title: Name → need link
strategies.description: Write one sentence: “When I did/experienced __, the need was __.”

strategies.title: Five gratitudes by need
strategies.description: List five gratitudes and tag each with the need it tended.

strategies.title: Parking-lot note
strategies.description: Make a note titled “Parking Lot” and park one worry there.

strategies.title: One next tiny step
strategies.description: Choose the smallest next step on something and do only that.

strategies.title: Calendar one thing
strategies.description: Add just one gentle, specific item to your calendar.

strategies.title: Mark a date on a calendar
strategies.description: Circle a meaningful upcoming date (rest day, call, walk).

strategies.title: Name support options
strategies.description: List three people or places you could ask for support when ready.

strategies.title: Self-check scale
strategies.description: Draw a 0–10 line for energy; mark where you are now.

strategies.title: Body scan (30 sec)
strategies.description: Scan from toes to head naming neutral sensations only.

strategies.title: Three shapes doodle
strategies.description: Draw one circle, one triangle, one square repeatedly for a minute.

strategies.title: Trace your hand
strategies.description: Outline your hand and write a need in each finger.

strategies.title: One-foot balance
strategies.description: Stand on one foot near support for 20–30 seconds.

strategies.title: Breath with steps
strategies.description: Take ten steps; inhale for two steps, exhale for three.

strategies.title: Name what’s within control
strategies.description: List three things within your influence today.

strategies.title: Name what’s outside control
strategies.description: List three things outside your influence today.

strategies.title: Choose a gentler word
strategies.description: Replace one harsh word in your self-talk with a kinder one.

strategies.title: Future-walk sketch
strategies.description: Pick a nearby block on a map and sketch a simple future walking loop.

strategies.title: Micro boundary
strategies.description: Say “No, thank you” to one low-stakes ask today.

strategies.title: Value compass card
strategies.description: Write five values/needs on a card/note you can glance at.

strategies.title: Two-sentence story
strategies.description: Write a two-sentence story about today from your own point of view.

strategies.title: Read one paragraph
strategies.description: Read one paragraph from any nonfiction page you have nearby.

strategies.title: One gentle stretch chain
strategies.description: Reach up, fold forward, roll up—three times, slowly.

strategies.title: Senses first aid kit
strategies.description: List one favorite sight, sound, taste, touch, and smell you can access easily.

strategies.title: Name a want & a don’t
strategies.description: Complete: “I want __ and I don’t want __ because I value __.”

strategies.title: Three breaths before reply
strategies.description: Take three breaths before sending your next message.

strategies.title: Put it on paper
strategies.description: Write a worry on paper and place it in an envelope or book.

strategies.title: Choose a supportive spot
strategies.description: Move to a seat with back support or softer light.

strategies.title: Micro-celebration
strategies.description: Clap once or do a tiny fist-pump after finishing a task.

strategies.title: Name one help to ask
strategies.description: Write a concrete, doable request you could ask someone this week.

strategies.title: Return to body cue
strategies.description: Set a simple cue (e.g., every doorframe = one deep breath) for today only.
